$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+3y \\ 2x-y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$" :question/worked-solution "Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -14 & -14\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{7}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-197649b0-e179-5dbc-96a2-7c730a9f52c3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$

$$

$$

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -3 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=2{R}_{2}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

"The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & -5 & -9 \\ 3 & b & 6 \\ 1 & \frac{4}{3} & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+y+z \\ x+z \\ y-z\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -3 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=2{R}_{2}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 & -9 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=-5,$ $b=3,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=-5+3+2=0.

:question/problem "The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & -5 & -9 \\ 3 & b & 6 \\ 1 & \frac{4}{3} & c\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -3 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=2{R}_{2}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 & -9 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=-5,$ $b=3,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=-5+3+2=0.
$$"] ["question-5979cff9-340a-5b78-84fd-5ca3a8c1f370" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-9715d32b-de54-5e1d-b216-07bf1e7e3fc2" :answer-field/id #uuid
